capacity.source: Prospectus (Sep 2026) and Q1 FY27 call (Oct 2026)

capacity.today: 345 tonnes of steam an hour in seven boilers (six owned, one leased): Ankleshwar 120, Vapi 60 coal + 15 waste-to-energy, Sarigam 60, Panoli 60, Nandesari 30; 60km of pipelines. It also resells steam bought at Sachin (from the promoter's Sanjoo Dyeing) and Dahej
capacity.utilisation: 41.4% in Q1 FY27 (40.9% FY26, 37.1% FY25), on 330 days at 80% load; Vapi waste-to-energy 78%, Ankleshwar 52–55%, Nandesari 53%, Vapi coal 29%, Sarigam about 13%, Panoli 7% (started June 2025). Management sees 60–65% as optimum; about 70% of capacity is contracted (ICRA says 87%)
capacity.fullUse: Not disclosed in rupees; existing plants add 5–10% volume a year as they fill
capacity.capexStatus: Four boilers (Jhagadia, Nandesari-2, Vapi-3, Pirana; 120 tonnes an hour) for FY27, Tarapur (60) in Q4 FY28 and three IPO-funded boilers (180) in Q1 FY29, taking capacity to 705; about ₹230cr still to spend, and spending on the four under construction is already 17–105% above budget
capacity.source: Prospectus (Sep 2026), Q1 FY27 presentation and call (Oct 2026)

capacity.today: 3,304 cancer beds of capacity, 2,855 operational and 2,440 revenue beds (including chemo day-beds) at 26 hospitals (25 in India plus Nairobi), with 38 radiotherapy machines (Q1 FY27)
capacity.utilisation: 58% 'centre utilisation' in FY26 (South 68%, West 50%, East 57%); HCG no longer reports occupancy, which CARE put at 68.7% in H1 FY26. About 400 built beds are not yet in use
capacity.capexStatus: About 188 beds in FY27, 520 in FY28–29 and 230 in FY30, to about 3,670 operational beds; bed capex about ₹150cr in FY27, ₹300cr over FY28–29 and ₹100cr in FY30, plus about ₹100cr a year of maintenance. Whitefield slipped to end-FY28 and Cuttack and Vizag to FY28–29; ₹75cr spent in Q1 FY27
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 presentation and call (Aug 2026), Q4 FY26 call, CARE (Jan 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Optical fibre 28 mn fibre-km and cable 39 mn fibre-km a year, including a ribbon-cable (IBR) line of about 14 mn fibre-km; no own preform (buys about 1,000 t a year); data-centre assembly and defence capacity not disclosed
capacity.utilisation: Fibre and cable both fully used (September 2026); management says it is choosing which orders to turn down
capacity.fullUse: Not disclosed; FY26 sales were about 4.1 times net block
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹1,800cr for fibre (to 43.1 mn fkm) and cable (to 62.0) by July 2028 and a 600 t preform plant by October 2028, plus ₹215cr for data-centre assemblies and ₹230cr for a grenade plant; guidance of ₹640cr for FY27 and ₹615cr for FY28 predates ₹1,220cr of later approvals; ₹436cr spent in H1 FY27; funded by internal cash, debt and promoter warrant money
capacity.source: NSE filings 4 August and 14 September 2026, Q1 FY27 call (Jul 2026) and Q2 FY27 results (Oct 2026)

capacity.today: Preform, fibre, cable and connectivity capacity not disclosed since April 2026; fibre at Aurangabad and Jiangsu (China), cable and connectivity at Silvassa, Dadra, Dello (Italy) and Lugoff (South Carolina); preform made in-house. Fibre was about 50 mn fibre-km in 2023, the last public figure
capacity.utilisation: About 70% blended (3 September 2026 filing); management says it now picks orders by capacity, and germanium and helium supply also limits orders
capacity.fullUse: Not disclosed; the ₹20,000cr FY29 target on +50% capacity would need near-full use and much more value per unit (₹4,750cr in FY26)
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹1,000cr a year for three years (₹3,000cr to end FY29) for +50% preform, fibre and cable and a greenfield connectivity plant in India, from accruals and/or debt (doubled from ₹500cr a year in July); plus up to $100m over five years for a US connectivity plant
capacity.source: NSE filing and investor day (3 September 2026), Q1 FY27 call (Jul 2026), Q4 FY26 call and Outlook Business (Oct 2023)

capacity.today: Asset-light global network for less-than-container-load (LCL) consolidation, whole-container (FCL) forwarding and air freight, about 80–85% of it outside India; it hires container space from shipping lines and works through contracted warehouses, so there is no plant capacity
capacity.utilisation: No figure; management works on fuller containers and fewer loss-making trade lanes, and says about 12–15% more volume from here would bring returns back to normal (Q1 FY27)
capacity.capexStatus: No expansion announced; asset-light services business where capex is 'a tiny fraction' of the P&L. Near-term growth by hiring teams for new products and markets, not acquisitions
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026)

capacity.today: One plant at Hariyala, Kheda (Gujarat): SteriPort IV bottles 11.6 crore a year after Line 3 (6.6 crore before, +75%; the Q1 FY27 call had said 'roughly 12 crore'); conventional IV fluids (LVP) 5.7 crore units; small-volume (SVP) blow-fill-seal lines
capacity.utilisation: SteriPort about 91% before Line 3 and plants about 96% (sector note); the Q1 FY27 call spoke of 90–95%
capacity.fullUse: Line 3 adds about ₹110–120cr of revenue a year at full use (Nov 2026 filing); management guides FY27 revenue about ₹370cr and FY28 about ₹425cr with all lines live
capacity.capexStatus: SteriPort Line 3 (₹90cr, about ₹80cr spent by August) commissioned September 2026; SVP line (about ₹30cr, ₹7cr spent by August) due March 2027; 10.8 MW captive solar plant commissioned June 2026, saving about ₹9cr a year
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026), Nov 2026 results filing and sector note

capacity.today: 612 wind-turbine towers a year (towers up to 140 metres): Koppal, Karnataka about 420 a year (35 a month) and Kutch, Gujarat about 192 a year (16 a month, about 60,000 t), Kutch operating since March 2026. A tower-internals plant at Koppal is being built up
capacity.utilisation: About 48% in FY26 (210 towers made, against 135 in FY25)
capacity.capexStatus: Kutch plant built in FY26 (₹97cr invested in the year) and now going through customer approvals and certification; no further plant announced. The August 2026 IPO money mostly repays the loans taken for it
capacity.source: Investor conference outcome (Oct 2026), Q1 FY27 presentation (Aug 2026) and IPO papers

capacity.today: About 1,400–1,600 t a year of APIs and intermediates in all: Anlon's own Rajkot plant 400 t, the rest at the acquired Apiqo Organics and Bizotic Lifesciences plants
capacity.utilisation: Q1 FY27: 62.37% on a consolidated basis per the presentation (the MD said about 65–70%); Anlon's own 400 t plant is full; Apiqo and Bizotic can run higher, but gradually
capacity.fullUse: Management targets ₹350–400cr of revenue in FY27 from today's plants and about ₹700cr in FY28 if the new 1,200 t plant starts on time
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹130cr expansion adding 1,200 t at Anlon's own site (to about 1,600 t), funded with about ₹70cr of debt and the rest from internal money, due by Q1 FY28; Apiqo capacity increase being explored
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: One precision-machining plant (Unit 1) in Bengaluru, about ₹30cr of sales a year; Unit 2 at the Hitech Defence and Aerospace Park, Devanahalli, twice its size, starting up (8 of the first 25 machines had arrived by June 2026)
capacity.utilisation: Unit 1 fully used (MD, June 2026); it turns work away for lack of capacity
capacity.fullUse: About ₹30cr a year from Unit 1; ₹90–100cr a year with Unit 2 full in FY28
capacity.capexStatus: Unit 2: about ₹60cr of machines, inspection equipment and software from the March 2026 IPO money; partial production from August 2026, all machines by about December 2026, full in FY28. A Unit 3 for assemblies and value-added work (land identified, 'up to another ₹70cr-plus' of sales) has no cost or date yet; the ₹500cr-a-year revenue goal for FY31 needs it
capacity.source: H2 FY26 call (5 Jun 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Asset-light: owns no plants but locks in about 9 million t a year of contract-manufacturing capacity (stone aggregates, ready-mix concrete and now asphalt) through deposits and exclusive long-term deals with plants in Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra; also B2B material supply through 2,200-plus vendors and a developer-services (DaaS) arm
capacity.utilisation: About 65–70% of the contract-manufacturing capacity used in Q1 FY27; about 8.65 lakh t of materials delivered in the quarter
capacity.capexStatus: No capex of its own: plans 2–3 million t a year more contract capacity (stone aggregates, southern Tamil Nadu) over the next two quarters by recycling existing deposits, to about 11 million t. DaaS portfolio over ₹2,750cr of project value after the ₹250cr Transcon mandate (27 Oct 2026)
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and NSE filing (27 Oct 2026)

capacity.today: Two plants at Mandi Gobindgarh, Punjab: about 1.2 lakh t a year in all (about 54,500 t of melting/foundry and finished-steel processing at Facility 1 and a 65,000 t rolling mill at Facility 2, per the RHP; IPO notes give 119,464 t or 119,690 t)
capacity.utilisation: 90.5% in Q1 FY27: melt shop 94%, rolling mill 87.5%; melting has run in the mid-90s for almost two years (FY26 overall about 88%)
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹80cr of capex in FY27 (₹5cr spent in Q1): IPO-funded machining and melting upgrades at both plants (₹56cr plus about ₹7cr rooftop solar), the new Unit 3 roll foundry and a ground-mounted solar plant from profits. No new melting capacity this year; it comes next year with Unit 3
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026) and RHP (Aug 2026)

capacity.today: More than 1,708 ISO tank containers (taken on lease-purchase) and over 100 container trailers at June 2026; branches in Hyderabad, Chennai, Delhi, Jaipur, Visakhapatnam, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Gandhidham, Ahmedabad, Indore, Nellore and Tada
capacity.utilisation: Q1 FY27: ISO tank containers about 83–84% (the MD: above 70% is very good); vehicles more than 90%, always short, so trucks are hired from outside
capacity.capexStatus: No plant or capital project announced; tank containers added as demand comes on lease-purchase (EMI) without upfront spending, vehicles added only for new branches, number not fixed. Growth from new branches in India and abroad (Thailand and Vietnam next) and moves into dry containers and project cargo
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Jul 2026)

capacity.today: A people business, about 97,000 staff: facility and food services (about 55% of revenue), security (almost 25,000 guards at June 2026, 900 added in Q1), telecom and industrial maintenance, STEAG India's power-plant operation and maintenance (about 14–16 GW of mostly thermal plants), and LSG's Bengaluru airline kitchen
capacity.utilisation: Not measured as capacity; the LSG Bengaluru kitchen can grow 15–20% a year and reach its maximum capacity in a couple of years (management)
capacity.capexStatus: No plant or capacity project: asset-light services. Growth comes from acquisitions, funded mainly by debt: STEAG India (completed 21 May 2026; four new five-year contracts worth over ₹5,100cr, three live from 1 July, the fourth from August) and LSG Sky Chefs' Bengaluru operations (about ₹110cr of revenue a year; closing expected in August 2026); management aims for net debt below 1 times EBITDA by March 2027
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Three plants: Thirumudivakkam, Chennai (wind-turbine yaw and pitch drives), Mannur near Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu, and Talegaon near Pune (gear motors, gearboxes and construction-equipment drives); about 3.41 lakh units made in FY25 (IPO documents); capacity measured in machine hours (about 11.2 lakh in FY24)
capacity.utilisation: About 75% across the plants in January–June 2026 (73.7% in CY2025, 64% in CY2023); nine months to September 2025: Thirumudivakkam 83.8%, Talegaon 75.9%, Mannur 73.6%
capacity.capexStatus: Plans a heavy-duty industrial gearbox plant next to Talegaon from its own cash, 'in the coming years'; cost, size and date not given. The IPO was all a sale by the parent, so no money came to the company
capacity.source: IPO offer documents as reported (DRHP Feb 2026, RHP Oct 2026); no results call held yet

capacity.today: A railway systems contractor (signalling, telecom, overhead electrification) with no factory; executable order book about ₹860cr plus GST (over ₹1,000cr with GST, including L1 positions) in May 2026, plus about ₹350cr of new orders in the first 45 days of FY27; orders take 18–24 months (up to 30) to execute
capacity.utilisation: Not measured; aims to win about ₹1,000cr of new orders in FY27 and open FY28 with about ₹1,000cr in hand
capacity.capexStatus: No plant project. About ₹15cr to be put into the NOVA subsidiary in FY27 (mostly capital spending, from internal cash) to develop its own Kavach train-protection system and other safety products
capacity.source: Q4 FY26 call (May 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Five Tier III data centres (Nashik, Navi Mumbai, Bengaluru, Mohali, Noida) with about 75,266 sq ft; 600–800 GPUs of its own; plus an 8,200-GPU (Nvidia B300) cluster in Australia whose capacity it buys from SharonAI and resells to one overseas customer
capacity.utilisation: No utilisation figure given
capacity.capexStatus: Own GPUs to rise to about 1,500 by January–February 2027 with IPO money, billing from Q1 FY28; ₹576cr of the ₹720cr IPO is earmarked for cloud and data-centre equipment, none used by September 2026; management plans about ₹3,000cr of capex in all including the GPU build-out, funded by customer advances, debt and IPO money in roughly equal parts; the Australian cluster is a pass-through commitment of about US$1.25bn over five years, not ESDS's own capex
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026) as recorded in the sector note, Q2 FY27 results (Nov 2026)

capacity.today: Owns no factory: its wall panels and laminates are made by 36–44 contract manufacturers in India, South Korea, China and elsewhere and sold through about 200 distributors and its acquired retailers (Uro Veneer World and Chawla Brothers, 51% each)
capacity.utilisation: No figure; asset-light design-and-brand model
capacity.capexStatus: No plant of its own; growth is by buying dealers and makers from internal cash. On 5 Nov 2026 it agreed to buy 51% of Drashti Surfaces, a veneer and decorative-laminate maker, for ₹31.1cr plus a loan of up to ₹20cr, its first in-house manufacturing. The ₹42.7cr Fabwood deal (56%) was put on hold on 26 Oct 2026
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026) and NSE filings (26 Oct and 5 Nov 2026)

capacity.today: Software delivery from its own campus in Mysuru (Hootagalli industrial area), with growing 'nearshore' teams placed near clients in the US, Canada and the UK. Headcount and seats are not given in the call
capacity.utilisation: Not given as a figure; management says the new nearshore teams start at lower utilisation and margins should recover as it rises (Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 16.2% against the 24–25% FY27 guide)
capacity.capexStatus: IPO (November 2025) money set aside for the Mysuru property: ₹61.77cr to buy land and put up a new building and ₹39.51cr to upgrade the existing facility, including external electrical systems; plus ₹54.64cr for IT hardware, software and networks. Progress and dates were not given on the call. Also looking at acquisitions in the US and India
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026), IPO prospectus (objects of the issue, Nov 2025) and sector note

capacity.today: Turnkey builder of pharma, vaccine and biotech plants; makes process, air and water systems and isolators in-house and with partners (including promoter-group firms). No plant capacity is disclosed; the company measures itself by its open order book, over ₹900cr (Q2 FY27 call; June 2026 also over ₹900cr), with a 'hot' pipeline of ₹3,600–4,000cr (₹3,800cr+ in July)
capacity.utilisation: Not applicable; Q2 FY27 revenue fell 24% to ₹92cr as large orders were delayed by the Gulf war, none cancelled
capacity.capexStatus: No plant or capacity expansion announced; asset-light project business. IPO money goes to working capital, general purposes and acquisitions, to be used by the end of FY27: a majority stake in SACE, a Saudi contractor, is done (first civil order won); a European (Italian) acquisition is in due diligence, to close within about six months or in the first quarter of next year (Q2 FY27 call)
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (Oct 2026), Q1 FY27 call (Jul 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Solar panels 3.5 GW (about 1.6 GW at the older plants plus 2 GW at Ratlam, started 14 May 2026); inverters and other power electronics 4 GW (including 2 GW at Ratlam, started August 2026); Mono-PERC solar cells 1 GW; lithium-ion batteries 500 MWh at Greater Noida. The 1.3 GWh tubular battery plant at Bawal was destroyed by fire on 6 May 2026; it now buys tubular batteries outside
capacity.utilisation: Cell plant above 80%; panel plants other than Ratlam about 70–80% (Q1 FY27 call, 14 Aug 2026). Ratlam runs one shift for now; management expects about 40–50% use of the Ratlam capacity this year
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹500cr of capex in FY27 (₹200cr debt, about ₹100cr of remaining IPO money, the rest own cash), taking gross block including work in progress from about ₹800cr to about ₹1,300cr: the Ratlam lithium-ion lines (2 GWh plus 1 GWh, due Q2 FY27), a 1.2 GW TOPCon cell line (₹350cr, Q1 FY28), a 1 GWh tubular battery plant at Hathras (₹20cr, Q3 FY27), plus a solar park and BESS. Separately about ₹180–200cr in the 50%-owned Zayo component companies (Fujiyama's equity about ₹50cr). No new equity planned this year
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026), board filings of 26 May and 25 Aug 2026, IPO prospectus (Nov 2025)

capacity.today: 8 IVF hubs and 28 spokes in 9 states (Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Patna, Ludhiana, Srinagar and others) before the FY27 openings, plus referral spokes starting in Paris, Nigeria and Sydney; South Extension (Delhi) hub opened 16 July 2026 as the first of 19 new hubs
capacity.utilisation: No figure given
capacity.capexStatus: 19 new IVF hubs from IPO money and internal accruals: 10 in FY27 (about ₹25cr, about ₹2.5cr a hub), 8 in FY28 and 1 in FY29; each said to break even in about three months. Board approved a women's hospital at Lucknow (up to ₹15cr from internal accruals), commercial in FY28–FY29
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Older mint and clove (eugenol) plants (standalone business), plus the new multi-purpose Krystal Ingredients plant at Dahej: cooling agents (Gemcool 3, 5 and 23) about 500 t a year, Safranal and phenol derivatives
capacity.utilisation: No figure for the older plants; for cooling agents management said it should be 'fairly close' to an analyst's 25% of 500 t in FY27 (Q1 FY27 call)
capacity.fullUse: Management expects Krystal products to be more than 50% of total revenue in FY28; no FY27 guidance
capacity.capexStatus: Dahej plant about ₹270cr, nearly ₹265cr already spent and mostly capitalised (depreciation ₹9.1cr a quarter); no new expansion announced
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (14 Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: One factory at Vile Bhagad (Mangaon, Maharashtra MIDC) making about 130 facade panels a day on four production lines, with its own NABL-accredited test rig; about 32,000 sq m built on an owned 1 lakh sq m plot (about 30% used)
capacity.capexStatus: Building an in-house glass processing unit at the same site (₹80cr: ₹50cr from the September 2026 IPO, the rest internal accruals), commissioning from about June 2027. Management says the factory can carry the next couple of years' growth with no other capex; with the glass unit the plot will be about 55–60% used, leaving room to expand
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Oct 2026) and IPO prospectus (Sep 2026)

capacity.today: An asset-light freight forwarder that books space on others' ships and planes: 21,841 containers (TEUs) handled in Q1 FY27 (26,278 a year earlier, 31,402 in Q4 FY26). Own fleet of 80 vehicles at June 2026 (42 at March 2026, 17 at December 2025), plus a small new warehousing line
capacity.capexStatus: Spending the IPO's ₹132.54cr on its own trucks, trailers and containers, all by March 2027: 42 trailers added in Q1 FY27, containers deployed from Q3 FY27. The monitoring agency (CRISIL) reported the IPO money used as planned
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and IPO prospectus (Sep 2025)

capacity.today: Several plants in Gujarat making both technicals (active ingredients, 70-plus, in multi-product plants; about 25% of revenue) and formulations (200-plus products; about 75%); a backward-integration technical plant at Saykha, Dahej was capitalised in Q1 FY27
capacity.utilisation: Technical plants about 70–75%; formulation plants about 25–30% (built for the peak season, not a bottleneck) (Q1 FY27 call)
capacity.capexStatus: No new plant announced; growth fits in existing plants, partly by swapping multi-product lines to high-value, low-volume molecules. The March 2026 IPO money went to repaying loans
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: About 31.5 mn sq ft of completed warehouses and factory buildings (October 2026; 28.5 mn sq ft at March 2026) across 46 assets in 10 markets, on 2,300 acres of fully paid land with about 29 mn sq ft more to build; 17 in-city sites (6.9 mn sq ft) of which only about 0.79 mn sq ft operates
capacity.utilisation: Stabilised occupancy about 94% (Q2 FY27, 95% before the new deliveries); a little over 1 mn sq ft of newly delivered space not yet let
capacity.fullUse: Contracted rent run-rate about ₹1,004cr a year (October 2026; ₹967–970cr at June), on 94% stabilised occupancy and about 2 mn sq ft of pre-commitments
capacity.capexStatus: FY27 target 6 mn sq ft delivered (2.7 mn in H1) and 6.5 mn sq ft leased (4.4 mn in H1), taking the network to nearly 35 mn sq ft by March 2027; about 6 mn sq ft of in-city centres over 3–4 years, first at Pimpri (Pune) in Q4 FY27; planned capex ₹1,500–2,000cr over three years (prospectus), new buildings mostly financed by construction loans; acquisitions to restart within a quarter or two
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (Oct 2026), Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Six plants (two at Shirwal near Pune, two at Pithampur, one at Nashik, one at Thane) on about 8 acres; hydraulic fitting capacity about 483 lakh pieces a year and captive forging about 3,120 t a year (company presentation); making about 35 lakh fittings a month
capacity.utilisation: About 60–70% (CMD, Q1 FY27 call); the company keeps 20–25% spare capacity so it can take new OEM orders
capacity.fullUse: About ₹200cr of sales today; the CMD says the ₹30cr IPO capex takes this to about ₹300–320cr (about ₹100cr more)
capacity.capexStatus: ₹30cr of IPO money for new machines (including automatic rotary transfer machines) in the existing plants, to be done within a year; a 6.5-acre automated plant approved by the board, ready in about two years, cost to be shared in November 2026
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026), company presentation and sector note

capacity.today: Four plants in Palghar, Maharashtra making nutraceuticals (tablets, capsules, powders, gummies, protein bars), cosmetics, Ayurvedic, pet-care and home-care products; a new tablet granulation line of about 480 kg a day (about 24,000 bottles a day); pet care making 16–18 t a month, going to about 25 t a month
capacity.utilisation: Nutraceuticals about 72%, cosmetics about 55%, pet supplements about 75% (MD, Q4 FY26 call, May 2026)
capacity.fullUse: The MD aims for ₹450–500cr of revenue by FY29 once the new plant fills (FY26: ₹147cr)
capacity.capexStatus: New 75,000 sq ft nutraceutical plant (enlarged from 35,000 sq ft, with ₹10cr of IPO money moved to it) to add about 2.5 times today's capacity, due August 2026 per the 10 July update; Olahey Wellness ready-to-drink beverage lines (about 10,000 bottles an hour) around the same time; a 1,000 kg an hour pet-food extrusion line ordered (from 100–150 kg an hour). ₹13.84cr of IPO capex money used by March 2026
capacity.source: Q4 FY26 call (May 2026), business update (10 Jul 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: An asset-light distributor and solution integrator of enterprise cybersecurity, data-centre, cloud and data-management technology. It measures itself by gross sales (₹641cr in Q1 FY27), its top 15 technology makers (about 74% of gross sales) and recurring (annuity) business (46.4% of gross sales). Revenue started in Vietnam, the Philippines and the Middle East in Q1 FY27
capacity.capexStatus: No expansion or plant; asset-light services business. The Centre of Excellence gets steady, small spending, with no extra capex in FY27 over earlier years
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Jul 2026)

capacity.today: Three recycling plants at Gummidipoondi (SIPCOT), Tamil Nadu, for copper, lead and aluminium scrap: about 3.08 lakh t a year combined per the IPO papers (July 2025). New copper lines: anode 1,600 t a month (two furnaces) and cathode 750 t a month since 5 Nov 2026 (1,500 t a month installed when complete). Lead volume about 1.85 lakh t in FY26
capacity.utilisation: No plant-wide figure given; anode line ramping up (about 600 t sold since start), cathode just started
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹87cr of capex in FY27, mostly copper value-added lines (cathode, wire rod, busbar and profiles), antimony and a ₹15cr plastic plant; Ahmedabad copper JV in trials; Kuwait investment held up by shipping; 15–20% more lead capacity awaits approval
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026), NSE filing (5 Nov 2026) and IPO papers

capacity.today: 25.1 MTPA of cement and GGBS grinding after the 1 MTPA Nagaur unit in October 2026 (24.1 MTPA before): Vijayanagar about 6.0, Dolvi 4.5, Nandyal 4.2, Salboni 3.6, Nagaur 3.5, Jajpur 1.5, Sambalpur 1.0, rest (Shiva) about 0.8 (FY25 annual report and company site, plus later additions). Clinker 9.74 MTPA including the Fujairah (UAE) joint venture: Nagaur 3.3, Nandyal 2.81, Shiva and Fujairah the rest
capacity.utilisation: Nagaur 75% in Q2 FY27 (55% in Q1, 68% in June). Company-wide cement capacity 61% in Q1 FY27 (no regional split given); clinker 61% including Nagaur, 87% without it (Q1 FY27). Sales were 3.93 million t in Q2 FY27, up 26%
capacity.capexStatus: Capex ₹2,300cr in FY27 (₹820cr of cash spent in H1; the full year's spend should be ₹2,200–2,300cr) and ₹2,000cr in FY28; about ₹7,500cr from here to reach 43.5 MTPA, then a vision of 68 MTPA. Net debt ₹4,287cr at September, 3.2 times EBITDA against the board's 3-times limit; the CFO expects it around 3 for about a year more. New in October 2026: ₹1,078cr approved for 2 MTPA each at Vijayanagar (GGBS, May 2028) and Dolvi (October 2028); Shiva Cement to merge into the company (5 shares for every 41)
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (Oct 2026), board outcome 27 Oct 2026, Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026), FY25 annual report

capacity.today: About 2.8 GWp of solar and wind running plus about 600 MWh of batteries (2,844 MWp and 603 MWh at 22 October 2026). Portfolio about 11.2 GWp plus 9 GWh of batteries, of which 6.1 GWp is operating or under signed PPAs; 84% is firm-power (FDRE) and hybrid
capacity.utilisation: Fleet load factor (CUF) 27% in Q2 FY27 and 28.5% in H1 (24.1% in H1 FY26); wind about 50%; plant availability 98.7%, grid availability 99.5%. Curtailment about 2.5% of revenue last quarter, only on plants on temporary grid access
capacity.fullUse: Run-rate EBITDA about ₹1,900cr on today's 2.8 GWp; about ₹2,750cr on about 3.9 GWp at March 2027; about ₹4,500cr on about 6 GWp in FY28 (Q1 FY27 call)
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹19,000cr spent in all by 30 September 2026 (₹2,600cr in Q2, ₹3,800cr in H1); about ₹5,000cr more in H2 takes it to about ₹24,000cr by March 2027 (the Q1 FY27 call had said about ₹22,000cr). Net debt ₹11,600cr at September
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (2 Nov 2026), Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026), NSE filings of 22 and 31 Oct 2026

capacity.today: One wood-glue plant near Ahmedabad (Santej): 2,000 t a month, being raised to 3,500 t a month (about 80% done in August 2026)
capacity.utilisation: About 60–70% in Q1 FY27 (the MD said 'about 60%' and '65–70%' at different points); about 1,300 t a month on average, 2,400 t in the peak month of March 2026
capacity.fullUse: ₹600–650cr of revenue at 3,500 t a month (FY26 revenue ₹315cr)
capacity.capexStatus: Brownfield to 3,500 t a month for about ₹7cr, due Q2 FY27; a later greenfield plant (first 1,500 t a month, ₹45–50cr, half land) from internal cash for a ₹1,000cr revenue 'vision', no date. Debt-free with about ₹160cr of cash
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026)

capacity.today: Residential developer, mostly in Mumbai and Thane: about 14 mn sq ft of ongoing projects to be completed over FY27–FY29 (the Q1 FY27 call had said about 15 mn sq ft); about 18.4 mn sq ft delivered to date; 25 projects of about 25.1 mn sq ft under way at March 2025 (ICRA)
capacity.utilisation: H1 FY27 completions 2.37 mn sq ft (over 2,200 units) of the 5.5 mn sq ft FY27 target: 0.79 mn sq ft in Q1 and 1.58 mn sq ft in Q2
capacity.fullUse: Revenue is booked on completion: the 14 mn sq ft due over FY27–FY29 is when the profit gets recognised; FY27 pre-sales target about ₹6,500cr (H1 ₹2,587cr, about 40%)
capacity.capexStatus: Grows through redevelopment and joint developments rather than buying land: Ashok Nagar, Kandivali (2.8 acres, about ₹1,250cr of sale value) signed in Q1 FY27; FY27 launch pipeline about 5 mn sq ft worth about ₹7,800cr; the 16.67% minority in the Parkcity, Thane entities bought for ₹52.5cr (Nov 2026)
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (Oct 2026), Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026), NSE filing 2 Nov 2026 and sector note

capacity.today: 889,200 t a year installed across 13 plants (eight in Maharashtra at Boisar/Tarapur and Nagpur, four at Bhachau in Gujarat, one in Italy) at end-June 2026, excluding captive rolling and galvanising; solar structures about 492,000 t (about 16.8 GW) of it (sector note)
capacity.utilisation: No figure given by management; about 135,000 t sold in Q1 FY27, about 61% of capacity annualised (inferred); an analyst on the Q1 FY27 call put the usual range at 55–60%, and management says use rises in the second half (58–60% of a year's revenue)
capacity.fullUse: No figure given; FY27 revenue guided up 60–65% (about ₹6,900–7,100cr)
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹900cr of capex in FY26 and more this year: new Bhachau transmission-tower plant started (peak in 6–9 months); a rolling mill and a data-centre PEB plant being built at Bhachau (PEB ready by the start of FY28); a solar stamped-parts plant at Boisar; a multiproduct plant in Saudi Arabia (trials from December 2026). No project costs disclosed
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Oct 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Castings: Koppal about 1,10,000 t a year, Solapur close to 90,000 t (with the new 15,000 t two-part foundry for large castings), Rajpura about 25,000 t (about 2,200 t a month); pig iron from mini blast furnaces at Koppal and Hiriyur (close to 7 lakh t planned in FY27); alloy steel at Jejuri (about 3.5 lakh t, rolling 15,000 t a month); seamless tubes at Baramati and Ahilyanagar (1,88,704 t sold in FY26)
capacity.utilisation: Rajpura foundry 'totally sold out' (Q1 FY27); the new Solapur two-part foundry to reach 500–600 t a month of its 1,250 t within 1–1.5 years and full use a year after that; no company-wide figure
capacity.capexStatus: ₹600–700cr of capex in FY27 (₹274cr by September per the Q2 presentation, as reported), rising in later years; about ₹3,500cr of projects over the next four years (the sector note says ₹3,000–3,500cr): 35 MW solar and 12 windmills, Solapur two-part foundry, Rajpura expansion, Koppal oxygen plant and coal injection, Hiriyur pig-iron upgrade, Jejuri rolling, premium couplings, and three large ones (Koppal steel plant, Baramati expander mill, Koppal pellet plant and iron-ore mines). Aim: double castings and steel sales and take tubes to 3.5–4 lakh t
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026), Q2 FY27 presentation (Oct 2026, as reported) and sector note

capacity.today: Six NABH-accredited Ayurvedic hospitals with 223 beds (March 2026): Gurgaon 95–96, Pitampura (Delhi) 30, Jaipur 20 and 30, Udaipur 30, Lucknow 18; eight clinics run as day-care centres (four added after the IPO); its own GMP plant making about 80 medicines
capacity.utilisation: Beds 69% full overall in FY26; the older Delhi and Gurgaon hospitals above 90% (Gurgaon 90–100% per the July 2026 filing), the four newer ones 35–40%; about ₹8,400 of revenue per occupied bed a day
capacity.capexStatus: FY27 plan: beds from about 223 to 350–500 and 30 new super-specialty clinics; 1,500–2,000 beds and 100 clinics within three years; a 500-seat telemedicine centre in 1–1.5 years. A hospital costs about ₹2.5–3 lakh a bed (₹2.5–3cr for 100 beds), paid from own funds. Board approved a 60–100-bed Gurugram hospital (July 2026); a 25-bed luxury wellness centre in Delhi is planned
capacity.source: Q4 FY26 call (5 May 2026), NSE filing of 9 Jul 2026 and sector note

capacity.today: Seven plants in Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh weaving and finishing engineered nylon, polyester, aramid (Kevlar) and other technical fabrics and making finished defence products (parachutes, camouflage systems); no total capacity figure because output depends on the product mix
capacity.utilisation: About 55–60% (management, Q1 FY27 call), after a large capex came fully online in FY26; outdoor and lifestyle fabric capacity is not a constraint
capacity.capexStatus: No large capex planned for the regular business; maintenance capex of about 5–10% of gross block a year plus some debottlenecking. Possible capex for new technologies and business areas being explored, not yet firmed up
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Five operating units at Amritsar: general (tablets and injectables), oncology, cephalosporin, beta-lactam and biologics (100-litre line approved by CDSCO; a 500-litre line, five times larger, installed and awaiting approval); lines are EU GMP and PIC/S approved. A sixth unit for hormones due in November 2026
capacity.utilisation: General and oncology units about 75–80% used; cephalosporin and beta-lactam about 20–25%; biologics not yet selling (Q1 FY27 call)
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹185–195cr of capex (₹195cr in the presentation): hormone plant about ₹70cr (start November 2026), oncology expansion about ₹50cr (done by March 2027, +45–50% oncology capacity), bioequivalence studies ₹25–30cr; machinery and a little more space in the general unit add at least 20%. Biosimilar clinical trials need about ₹150cr between Q3 FY28 and Q4 FY29. Funded from cash flow; an extended loan is in place but unused. A planned partner oncology plant is on hold
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: 15.5 million pooled assets at September 2026 (13.8 million a year earlier), worth over ₹1,820cr: about 9.4 million wooden pallets plus plastic crates, containers and electric forklifts; 27 fulfilment centres (two closed after merging with CHEP sites) and 11,000-plus customer touchpoints
capacity.utilisation: Q2 FY27: pallets 89.3% (same as a year earlier; aim 90–91% over the coming quarters), containers 73.7% (71.7% a year earlier), forklifts 82.3%
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹450cr of capex in FY27 (₹213cr in H1), mostly new pallets, crates and forklifts, with about 850,000 more pallets in the pool; crate prices have nearly doubled, so crate additions are held back. ₹142cr cash purchase of Vimprotech (crate and container maker, two plants in Puducherry and Tamil Nadu) and TIPS (crate pooling, 0.25 million crates and trays), together ₹65cr of FY26 revenue, signed 26 Oct 2026. Gulf units (Saudi, UAE) licensed but deployment held back by the war; more acquisitions in India and the Gulf being looked at
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (Oct 2026), Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026) and 26 Oct 2026 filing

capacity.today: Machinery plants at Kanpur making tape extrusion lines, circular looms, winders, coating and lamination lines and bag-converting machines, with in-house machining, sheet-metal and electronics shops; capacity is shared across product lines and topped up by a large vendor base
capacity.utilisation: About 70–72% in Q1 FY27 (the CFO also said about 75% earlier in the call); about 80–85% is the practical ceiling
capacity.fullUse: About ₹2,400–2,500cr of revenue a year with some balancing of machines (FY26 revenue ₹1,717cr)
capacity.capexStatus: No expansion planned yet; only routine balancing and maintenance capex. Beyond ₹2,500cr of revenue, about ₹80–100cr of capex for every extra ₹500cr, which can be added in 5–6 months on land it already has next to the Kanpur works
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026)

capacity.today: Card plants in India (hub) with personalisation bureaus abroad (Nigeria) and 31 kiosks in Spanish airports: about 11.9cr cards a year installed (FY26, prospectus); metal cards 6.7 lakh a year (March 2026)
capacity.utilisation: Plastic cards about 75–80% used in Q1 FY27 (69% in FY26, prospectus); Nigeria personalisation bureau about 60%
capacity.capexStatus: ₹238cr of IPO money for capacity over three years, ₹100–120cr of it in FY27: at least triple metal-card capacity, tax stamps, base cards for exports, and personalisation bureaus in developed markets (about ₹30cr each, one more possibly this year). About ₹300cr spent on capex in the past two to three years
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (5 Oct 2026) and IPO prospectus (Sep 2026)

capacity.today: Granite: 16-plus Black Galaxy and Absolute Black mines with processing in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. Quartz: a first-phase processing plant that can go up to 18,000 t a month (15,000 t a month is the planned steady level)
capacity.utilisation: Quartz plant sold about 5,000 t in Q1 FY27 (about ₹5cr), about 1,700 t a month; aiming for 10,000 t a month by end-Q2 and 15,000 t a month by the year end; granite volume up about 10% in Q1 FY27
capacity.fullUse: Quartz at 15,000 t a month: about ₹180–200cr of revenue in FY28 (management)
capacity.capexStatus: Quartz phase 2 being built (about ₹125cr over FY27–FY28, from IPO money); Sri Lanka mineral-sands plant about ₹120cr, awaiting a licence; Indonesian rare-earth joint venture with PERMINAS, cost to come; Kerala rare-earth pilot with KMML is small and stalled. Granite capex is routine and paid from cash flow
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: One large plant at Perundurai near Erode, Tamil Nadu: paneer 150 t a day; natural cheddar cheese 120 t a day (started Q1 FY27; the Q2 FY27 call called it 100 t); Skyr and Greek yogurt 150 t a day (from 20 t, September 2026); protein-product capacity about 150–180 t a day; plus ice cream, curd, ghee, butter and whey lines
capacity.utilisation: Q2 FY27: paneer close to 65% (about 100 t a day made); cheddar cheese about 20%; yogurt 35–40 t a day made on 150 t (about 25%); the Q1 FY27 call put the plant at roughly half used overall
capacity.fullUse: Management says the Perundurai plant can make about 3–3.5 times FY26 revenue (₹3,138cr) at today's prices, and expects it to be fully used around 2030; paneer capacity full in 24–30 months
capacity.capexStatus: IPO money is funding the RHP projects (whey protein concentrate, lactose, natural cheese, yogurt and cream cheese lines; purchase orders placed); ₹40cr yogurt plant done; ₹70cr of work in progress and no big capitalisation planned; studying another 200 t/day of paneer at Perundurai; 50-acre site bought at Baramati, Maharashtra for a plant in about three years, no budget yet; ₹750cr of debt repaid, net debt ₹32.6cr at September 2026
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (Oct 2026), Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Ramming mass capacity 5.76 lakh t a year after the Purulia greenfield plant (Metalurgica) started commercial production on 10 October 2026, up from 2.56 lakh t; plants in West Bengal and Jharkhand (main Monolithisch plant, the MIGPL Ranchi plant) and the MIL Silvassa plant
capacity.utilisation: About 68–69% for the group in Q2 FY27 before the greenfield plant (about 55,000 t sold in the quarter): Ranchi about 90–95%, the main Monolithisch plant about 55–60%; the greenfield plant needs 8–10 months to ramp up
capacity.fullUse: Management guides ₹500–550cr of revenue in FY28 from the 5.76 lakh t plus mine surplus (FY26: ₹135cr); the two new regional plants should add about 3 lakh t at about ₹8–8.5 a kg, run at 85–90%
capacity.capexStatus: Purulia greenfield started 10 October 2026; Nawada, Bihar quartzite mine acquired (mining by a raising contractor, stone from early 2027, with a beneficiation and storage facility proposed); two regional plants for ₹45cr from internal cash: near Hospet, Karnataka (1.25 lakh t, ₹20cr, July 2027) and Udaipur, Rajasthan (1.75 lakh t, ₹25cr including about ₹6cr of land, November 2027), taking capacity to about 8.75 lakh t
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (Oct 2026), Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: An EPC contractor, not a factory business: builds overhead lines, substations (up to 220 kV, its largest a 400 kV GIS job at Dholera worth about ₹200cr) and underground cables, and maintains more than 100 substations and 400 km of lines. Order book ₹621cr at March 2026 (lines ₹449cr, substations ₹140cr, maintenance ₹21cr, cables ₹10cr), about ₹665–670cr after a ₹45cr GETCO order in April; it was ₹745cr in December 2025
capacity.utilisation: Not measured; orders take 12–24 months to execute (order book about 1.4 times FY26 revenue)
capacity.capexStatus: No plant or capacity project: asset-light EPC (44% return on capital in FY26). Part of the April 2026 IPO money goes to long-term working capital for bid deposits, guarantees and mobilisation
capacity.source: Q4 FY26 call (May 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: 8 own factories and 22 outsourced (contract) factories making MTR, Eastern and Rasoi Magic spices and ready-to-cook foods; sold through about 6.8 lakh retail outlets plus modern trade and quick commerce
capacity.capexStatus: No new plant or capacity expansion announced; spending goes on the Kerala distribution overhaul (foods done June 2026, open-format outlets by December 2026, spices by March 2027) and Project Bolt for digital commerce. The November 2025 IPO was an offer for sale, so it raised no money for capex
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Grid-battery (BESS) assembly at Bengaluru (subsidiary Lineage Power): 5 GWh a year on two 2.5 GWh lines (line 2 commissioned August 2026, doubling capacity from 2.5 GWh), with its own container fabrication unit (trial runs in August)
capacity.utilisation: No % given; H1 FY27 output 0.844 GWh (Q2 press release, as reported); 90-plus battery containers delivered in Q1 FY27 and 210 planned in Q2 (178 in all of FY26)
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹300cr for the whole BESS plant (the first 5 GWh, a third line of 5 GWh due December 2026 to make 10 GWh, and container fabrication), mostly land, funded from pre-IPO private placement money; planning battery-cell making (research centre in Pune, preparing a bid for the 10 GWh cell PLI), no cost given. Cells are still bought from China
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and 31 Oct 2026 results filing and press release

capacity.today: 3,960 operating beds at June 2026 in about 17 hospitals across north India (Gurgaon, Ambala, Mohali, Panchkula, Bhatinda, Agra and others); 4,290 after Rudrapur (330 beds) started on 2 August 2026
capacity.utilisation: Network occupancy 56% in Q1 FY27 (68% a year earlier; 64% in FY26), down because 960 beds were added in a year (Bhatinda 250, Agra 360, Panchkula 350); FY27 occupancy expected below FY26
capacity.capexStatus: Plan to reach 4,740 beds by March 2027 and 5,740 by March 2028; about ₹767cr of capex and acquisitions over FY27–FY28 (including Rudrapur and Panchkula) for 2,130 beds, about ₹36 lakh a bed, funded from internal cash and IPO money without material new debt
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Main plant at Manjusar GIDC, Vadodara (11–22kV ring main units, MV/LV and control panels, compact substations) plus a skill development centre; a rented 30,000–40,000 sq ft unit at Khordha, Odisha, started small jobs in 2026. Capacity in units is not disclosed
capacity.utilisation: Not disclosed
capacity.fullUse: Management: the two new plants can add about ₹300cr of revenue at full use (Karachiya GIS about ₹200cr, Odisha about ₹100cr), against FY26 revenue of ₹198cr
capacity.capexStatus: IPO-funded: ₹20cr for the Karachiya (Vadodara) GIS plant, due September 2026, and ₹19cr for Odisha, now in rented sheds to start fully by October 2026 (the own factory on 2.5 acres of allotted land had been planned for May 2027). By 30 September 2026 about ₹21.79cr had gone into the Gujarat GIS plant and ₹6.64cr into Odisha (H1 FY27 board meeting, as reported). Savings in Odisha may go to a later GIS expansion, after board approval
capacity.source: Q4 FY26 call (May 2026), H1 FY27 results board meeting (29 Oct 2026, as reported) and sector note

capacity.today: 54 Patel's R Mart stores (28 September 2026; 50 at March 2026) in Thane and Raigad districts, about 2.42 lakh sq ft of retail space; processing units at Ambernath and two in Kutch (pulses, spices, peanuts); Ambernath distribution centre 64,000 sq ft, being expanded to 84,000 sq ft
capacity.utilisation: Processing units 50–55% used (Q1 FY27 call), aiming for about 80–82% by the end of FY27–FY28; the Ambernath distribution centre ran full before its expansion
capacity.fullUse: A store sells about ₹80–90 lakh a month on average (₹80 lakh–₹1cr by size); mature stores about ₹20,000 per sq ft a year; new stores expected at about ₹1cr a month
capacity.capexStatus: 8–10 new stores in FY27 at about ₹5,000–6,000 per sq ft, paying back in about 24 months; ₹2cr from internal cash to add 20,000 sq ft at the Ambernath distribution centre (announced 30 Oct 2026, 15–20 days to finish)
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (24 Aug 2026), company filing of 30 Oct 2026 and sector note

capacity.today: Mostly online courses; offline: 353 offline and hybrid centres at March 2026 (198 a year earlier): Vidyapeeth classroom centres (about 70% of offline, batches of 80 students), smaller Pathshala hybrid centres, and subsidiaries Xylem (Kerala) and Utkarsh (Rajasthan)
capacity.utilisation: Offline seats used by about 1.99 students each (1.77 a year earlier), as centres run more than one batch per seat
capacity.capexStatus: Offline roll-out slowed: new centres to be decided over the next two quarters (from August 2026), only where centre economics work; offline near breakeven expected in FY27. Treasury about ₹5,600cr at June 2026 (including ₹2,000cr of IPO money), to go mainly to new online content and categories, organic or by acquisition, and AI tutoring
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Distilleries 450 KLPD in all: Indri (Haryana) 220 KLPD of grain spirit and ethanol plus 30 KLPD of malt, and the new Mahasamund (Chhattisgarh) distillery 200 KLPD (210 KLPD in the Q1 FY27 call). 87,000 filled barrels of maturing malt (about 1.6 crore litres) in August 2026. Sugar mill at Indri about 5,000 t of cane a day (company profile)
capacity.utilisation: Q1 FY27: malt plant about 80%, Indri distillery expansion about 60%; Chhattisgarh had only about 15 days of output (about ₹5cr of sales) and is guided to about 50% use by March 2027 (the Q4 FY26 call had said full use within about six months). The sugar mill crushed 54.21 lakh quintals of cane in 126 days in the 2024–25 season, about 4,300 t a day
capacity.fullUse: Management: 30 KLPD of malt makes 80–90 lakh litres a year, enough for about 8–8.5 lakh cases of Indri; FY27 revenue from the new capacity guided at ₹250–300cr extra from Indri and ₹300–400cr from Chhattisgarh
capacity.capexStatus: Heavy capex done (part of a ₹1,000cr three-year plan; ₹450cr spent by the FY25 annual report). FY27 capex no more than ₹25–30cr, mainly warehouses and some bottling; barrels (to more than 1,15,000–1,20,000 by March 2027) are bought as an ongoing expense. Scotland (Portavadie) distillery still to be built over the next couple of years. Debt not to rise in FY27, to fall from FY28
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026), Q4 FY26 call (Apr 2026), FY25 annual report and sector note

capacity.today: About 98,000 t a year across two plants: Khopoli about 78,800 t and Mahad (newer greenfield site) about 19,900 t; spare land of about 10–12 acres at Khopoli and 20 acres at Mahad (10 acres bought in September 2026)
capacity.utilisation: Khopoli ran at 'optimum' use in FY26; Mahad rose from about 13% in FY24 to 44% in FY26 and 60%-plus in Q1 FY27, with 70%-plus expected by March 2027
capacity.fullUse: Phase 1 (about 60,000 t more) should bring about ₹500–550cr of revenue at peak; management aspires to ₹2,800–3,000cr of revenue in five years (₹1,233cr in FY26)
capacity.capexStatus: Phase 1: ₹250–300cr over the next two years for existing products (₹50–60cr of it land and infrastructure), funded by internal money and possibly some debt; Phase 2: another ₹250–300cr for new R&D products, still at product selection, site preparation and approvals; more than ₹25cr on acetone storage at Khopoli over the next year
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Assembles UPS systems, inverters, lithium battery packs, stabilisers and transformers (much of the UPS range imported and customised) and resells batteries and IT hardware; builds solar and BESS projects. A 1.2 GWh BESS assembly plant at Jhajjar, Haryana and a UPS plant in Gujarat were both due to start in Q2 FY27. Order book ₹1,085cr at June 2026, of which ₹854cr is two BESS developer projects (Bihar 120 MWh, Karnataka 300 MWh)
capacity.utilisation: Not given for current plants; Jhajjar BESS plant to run at no more than about 25% in FY27 while it focuses on commercial and industrial buyers
capacity.fullUse: Jhajjar BESS plant at optimal use: a 14–15% EBITDA margin (management); an analyst put peak revenue at ₹1,000–1,200cr, not confirmed by management
capacity.capexStatus: Jhajjar 1.2 GWh BESS plant in the final stage of commissioning and Gujarat UPS plant progressing, both expected in Q2 FY27 (end of H1); BESS developer projects in subsidiary SPVs, Bihar debt being tied up with SBI; ₹43cr raised by preferential issue; more equity possible for major expansion
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Pernia's Pop-Up Shop: 12 experience centres in India (large stores of 20,000–60,000 sq ft in Mumbai and Delhi; Hyderabad too) plus London and New York (Madison Avenue, since March 2026), and a website listing about 2 lakh designer pieces from about 1,100 designers. Four large stores opened in FY26 (Fort and Linking Road in Mumbai, South Ex in Delhi, Madison Avenue)
capacity.utilisation: Not measured; FY27 is the four new large stores' first full year. Average order ₹86,000 in Q1 FY27 (₹76,000 in FY26)
capacity.capexStatus: No significant expansion planned for now (first call, 29 Sep 2026): management wants a full year from the four FY26 stores before deciding on more
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Maize crushing 1,650 t a day at Kishanganj, Bihar (doubled from 825 t on 26 May 2026), with a 180 t/day liquid glucose line, a 50 t/day maltodextrin powder line, modified-starch lines and a 15.8 MW cogeneration plant (from 7.1 MW)
capacity.utilisation: 71.4% in Q1 FY27, held down by nine shutdown days to connect the new lines (about 7,200 t of crushing lost); liquid glucose about 70%; Q1 crushing 69,689 t (64,770 t a year earlier); FY26 crushing 2.65 lakh t, FY27 target at least 4 lakh t
capacity.fullUse: Management says the new capacity is about half starch and half value-added products, so value-added would be about 30–35% of turnover at full use (3% in FY26, 20–22% guided for FY27)
capacity.capexStatus: The ₹664cr expansion is done (₹552cr spent by June 2026), funded mostly by Bihar-subsidised term loans; no new capex in FY27 while the plant stabilises; dextrose to start in Q4 FY27; management says it is too early to talk about the next expansion
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: About 8.51 lakh live rental items (furniture and appliances) at March 2026 for about 2.54 lakh subscribers in 29 cities, served from city warehouses and 89 company-run stores at June 2026 (82 in March); live items up 41% a year in Q1 FY27
capacity.utilisation: Items rented out ('occupancy') 85–86% in Q1 FY27, stable; management aims for about 83–84%, saying 90% means stock-outs and 65–70% idle stock
capacity.capexStatus: No plant or project: it grows by buying more items for rent each year (₹175cr of capex in FY26, of which ₹87.5cr was growth capex by management's account), funded from operating cash (₹173cr in FY26) and debt. The ₹150cr IPO (Sep 2026) repays ₹70cr of debt and pays ₹42.5cr of warehouse and store rents; none is earmarked for buying items
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Oct 2026) and IPO prospectus (Sep 2026)

capacity.today: Noida plant about 760 t of fragrances and flavours a year; the new YEIDA plant (trial production from September 2026) takes it to about 2,760 t, about four times
capacity.utilisation: About 124% of rated capacity in FY26, held at 120%+ in H1 FY27 until YEIDA starts
capacity.fullUse: No figure given; management guides revenue of ₹200cr in FY27, ₹250cr in FY28 and ₹300cr in FY29 (FY26 ₹152cr) and does not expect the new capacity to fill quickly
capacity.capexStatus: YEIDA plant about ₹184cr (₹76.59cr spent by March 2026: ₹28.79cr IPO money, ₹47.80cr own cash; about ₹60cr of debt to be drawn as needed); installed and commissioned, trial production from September 2026
capacity.source: Q4 FY26 call (Jun 2026), Oct 2026 filing and sector note

capacity.today: Leased plants: five in Mumbai (one more lease taken in FY26) and Pune (space raised about 25% in Q4 FY26), making shop fixtures for retail chains
capacity.utilisation: Over 90% used (sector note); existing space can still take about 30% more revenue (CFO, May 2026)
capacity.fullUse: About ₹284cr of revenue from today's space (FY26's ₹218cr plus about 30%, by arithmetic); about ₹500cr once the Ambernath plant runs, more with extra machines
capacity.capexStatus: Building its own 2,50,000 sq ft Ambernath plant from IPO money (about ₹90–95cr in all, ₹58–65cr spent by May 2026), due in Q3 FY27; the five leased Mumbai plants will move into it
capacity.source: Q4 FY26 call (May 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: 24 plants making and personalising bank cards (including metal and biometric cards), cheque books, secure mail, RFID tags and SIM cards, including units at Navi Mumbai, Okhla, Nagpur, Kundli and Bengaluru
capacity.utilisation: About 65–70% on average, reaching 85–90% at month-ends and in banks' card-renewal peaks; SIM cards about 40% (Q1 FY27 call, 24 Jul 2026)
capacity.capexStatus: About ₹140–160cr of capex a year, including FY27, from IPO money and cash. The 2025 IPO set aside ₹197.91cr for equipment at Navi Mumbai, Okhla, Nagpur, Kundli and Bengaluru (₹6.7cr used in Q1 FY27). A new greenfield metal-card plant in Bengaluru (50,000 sq ft) is due by December 2026 after approvals; a Nagpur facility is also under construction
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Jul 2026) and IPO prospectus (Sep 2025)

capacity.today: A building-materials retailer and distributor: about 96 stores and over 130 fulfilment centres, mostly in South India, selling about 1 million tonnes of steel in FY26 plus tiles, sanitaryware and other materials; manufacturing moved to a separate company in the demerger (January–February 2026)
capacity.utilisation: Not measured; Q1 FY27 volume grew about 10%
capacity.capexStatus: No plant project; capex is small (warehousing, cutting lines, stores). Three stores and fulfilment centres added in Q1 FY27 (Mangalore, Mumbai, Thrissur) and about five more guided for the rest of FY27 (8–9 for the year), into new territories including North and West India; acquisitions 'on the table'
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: 216 media assets at July 2026, mainly in Mumbai: 74 static hoardings and 142 digital LED time slots (including new premium sites at JVPD, Lower Parel and Infinity Mall), plus campaigns through 250-plus partners in 235-plus towns
capacity.utilisation: No figure disclosed
capacity.capexStatus: IPO (May 2026, ₹58cr fresh) funds ₹12.72cr of new LED screens and ₹5cr for a deal to sell space on 20 LED screens owned by Capital World Media Services; three Mumbai hoardings (Agadi MT, Nagda Pump House, JP Road) being converted to LED, announced July 2026. No results call held
capacity.source: IPO prospectus (May 2026), July 2026 company update and sector note

capacity.today: An asset-light freight forwarder: books cargo space on about 56 airlines under capacity contracts; moved 23,486 t of air freight in Q1 FY27 (about 6.2% of India's air exports); express arm handled 59,700 shipments across 31 locations in Q1; offices in Hong Kong, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Bangladesh, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the UK and Germany; also ocean freight, trucking and warehousing
capacity.utilisation: Not measured; air export volume grew 23% in Q1 FY27 against 3.8% for India
capacity.capexStatus: Routine group capex about ₹35–40cr a year (warehouses, offices); a pharma cold-chain warehouse due to start in Q3 FY27; ₹30cr approved (17 Sep 2026) for offices in five new Asian countries including China, Malaysia and the Philippines (only 10–15% of it capex) plus ₹20cr for existing offices in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Vietnam
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Steroid and hormone API plants at Rau and Pithampur (Indore), about ₹640cr of gross block at June 2026; a new 400-kilolitre fermentation (biotech CDMO) plant at Ujjain with a separate biologics (insulin) unit; a dual-chamber-vial injectables plant at Mhow (subsidiary Knovea)
capacity.utilisation: API plants about 70–80% (Q1 FY27 call, 22 Sep 2026). The 400 kL Ujjain fermentation capacity is largely booked under existing take-or-pay contracts ('Phase 0') but has no commercial revenue yet
capacity.fullUse: The API plants earn about ₹800–900cr of revenue a year today
capacity.capexStatus: More than ₹1,000cr already invested in the new Ujjain and Mhow plants, with revenue expected to start within 6–12 months of September 2026. Next: a 600 kL brownfield fermentation expansion ('Phase 1') at Ujjain, construction from Q3 FY27 over 15–18 months, part-funded by customers; capex of at least ₹200–250cr a year for two to three years. Q1 FY27 capex about ₹68cr
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Sep 2026), Q2 FY27 investor release and filing (Nov 2026)

capacity.today: 580 travel food outlets and lounges (system-wide) at 21 Indian airports at June 2026, with 153 brands, plus outlets in Malaysia and Hong Kong; 87 outlets and two lounges added in the 12 months to June, including Noida (opened Q1 FY27), Navi Mumbai, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad and Cochin; Bhogapuram airport opened on 17 August 2026 through its GHL joint venture
capacity.utilisation: Not measured as capacity; new outlets take 12–18 months to mature at running airports and about 24 months at new ones. System-wide like-for-like sales up 0.8% in Q1 FY27, net contract gains 15.9%
capacity.capexStatus: More than 50 outlets under development across the network, to open and mature over 12–18 months from August 2026; passenger services (meet-and-greet, porters) launched at Noida, to spread to other airports. Debt-free with about ₹970cr of cash. Delhi T3 leaves the consolidated accounts from October 2026; Chennai and Kolkata concessions come up for renewal in 2027
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Tile capacity of 50.6 million square metres a year (management), mostly glazed vitrified tiles from eight Morbi-area plants, plus the new Tezpur, Assam plant (Allemby Ceramics, about 50% owned); the RHP lists about 39 million square metres in its own plants, including the Solaris ceramic plant now shut. About 80% of sales are made in-house, the rest bought from contract makers
capacity.utilisation: 72% in FY26; 76% in H1 FY27 (63% in Q1 after April's gas shortage, 89% in Q2); aiming for 80–85% next year. Tezpur plant 50% in Q2 FY27, expected 75% in Q3
capacity.capexStatus: No immediate capex (first call, 23 Oct 2026); the Tezpur plant started production in H1 FY27 and the shut Solaris ceramic plant is to be converted to glazed vitrified tiles. IPO money (₹245cr) goes to repaying loans, not capacity
capacity.source: H1 FY27 results and presentation (19 Oct 2026), first call (23 Oct 2026, via sector note), RHP

capacity.today: Steel: ESL Steel at Bokaro about 1.7 MTPA of hot metal (presentation; the CFO said 1.6 on the Q2 call), making TMT bars, wire rod, ductile-iron pipes, billets and pig iron; the Goa pig-iron plant (VAB) with environmental clearance for 1.2 MTPA and its own met-coke plants; about 2.8 MTPA of hot metal across the two in FY26. Iron ore: Bicholim (Goa) 3 MTPA, plus mines in Karnataka and Odisha (capacity not given); 11.4 million wet t mined in FY26 (Karnataka 5.6, Goa 2.9, Odisha 2.9). Liberia: about 4 billion t of magnetite resources, no production
capacity.utilisation: No utilisation figure given. Hot metal made in H1 FY27: Bokaro 679 kt, Goa 474 kt (1,153 kt in all, up 3%), after planned shutdowns at both plants in Q2; record 568 kt of pig iron in H1. Iron ore saleable output 4.2 million dry t in H1 FY27 (Q2 1.5 million, down 13%; Karnataka down 49% under a revised mine plan, Odisha up 46%)
capacity.capexStatus: ₹3,697cr approved (ESL Phase 1A ₹2,975cr, Goa ductile-iron pipe plant ₹722cr); ₹2,796cr spent by 30 Sep 2026, ₹901cr left. About ₹300cr spent in H1 FY27 and ₹600–700cr planned in H2. Bokaro's completion waits for Stage II forest clearance ('on the verge of final approval', 27 Oct 2026), then 4–5 months. Later: Phase 2 to about 5 MTPA (tentatively about US$400m, not yet approved), Goa and Karnataka mine additions, and Liberia at detailed feasibility
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (27 Oct 2026), Q2 FY27 investor presentation, Vedanta FY25 release (VAB 1.2 MTPA clearance) and sector note

capacity.today: Gross operated output 72.2 kboepd in Q2 FY27 (Rajasthan 59.9, Ravva 8.1, the rest Cambay and OALP blocks), down 19% on a year; 77.7 kboepd in Q1 FY27 (Rajasthan 63.1, offshore 11.6, OALP 3.1). Working-interest output 47.8 kboepd in Q2 (51.1 in Q1). Rajasthan holds about 82% of reserves and resources; its licence runs to May 2030
capacity.utilisation: Not a capacity business: output is set by the fields' natural decline (Rajasthan down about 15% a year), slowed by polymer and chemical flooding, infill wells and well work; Cambay output down 83% after its licence extension was refused
capacity.capexStatus: FY27 output guidance 73–77 kboepd with capex of $320–340 million; about $200 million (about ₹2,000cr) of that for enhanced recovery in Rajasthan's Mangala, Bhagyam and Aishwariya fields (news report, Oct 2026); gas growth from a new north-east hub, no figure given
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 production update and results (Oct 2026, via news reports), Q1 FY27 call (Jul 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: 4,180 MW of coal plants: Talwandi Sabo, Punjab 1,980 MW (three 660 MW units, contracted to PSPCL to 2041); Meenakshi, Andhra Pradesh 1,000 MW; Jharsuguda, Odisha 600 MW (contracted to GRIDCO to 2037); Sakti, Chhattisgarh 600 MW (Unit 1), with a second 600 MW unit being built
capacity.utilisation: Q2 FY27: Talwandi Sabo availability 79% (90% a year earlier, 86% in Q1); Jharsuguda availability 98% (48% a year earlier); Meenakshi sold 1,470 million units with its full 1,000 MW restored (about 67% load, by arithmetic); Sakti Unit 1 down from a boiler accident on 14 April 2026 until a Sakti unit was synchronised on 25 October 2026. Total sales 5,593 million units, up 26%; about 74% of volume under medium and long-term contracts
capacity.capexStatus: Sakti Unit 2 (600 MW, ₹5,209cr budget, ₹1,745cr left to spend at June 2026) due by Q4 FY27, taking capacity to 4,780 MW; a further 7,200 MW planned from FY30 (not yet board-approved), aiming to be a top-three private thermal producer by FY33
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 results release (29 Oct 2026), Q1 FY27 call (Jul 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Copper and aluminium winding wires and strips in Gujarat: about 19,680 t a year before the expansion (prospectus); new ALCU Industries plant at Narsanda started 7 February 2026 with about 6,000–7,000 t installed by May 2026, the rest due by about Diwali to December 2026, taking the total to 35,000–36,000 t (prospectus: 37,680 t)
capacity.utilisation: No current figure; management expects 50–60% use of the total in FY27 and about 80% (its practical maximum) of 36,000 t in FY28. FY26 volume about 18,024 t; ALCU made about 800 t in February–March 2026
capacity.fullUse: No sales figure given; management expects EBITDA per tonne to rise with the new products
capacity.capexStatus: ALCU expansion funded with ₹140cr of IPO money, ₹124cr of it spent by 30 September 2026 (monitoring report); no further expansion decided, though there is land to grow
capacity.source: Q4 FY26 call (14 May 2026), IPO prospectus (Dec 2025), monitoring-agency report reviewed 4 Nov 2026

capacity.today: An EPC contractor for substations, transmission and distribution lines, solar plants and water schemes; order book about ₹6,496cr in August 2026 (solar 62%, T&D 28%, water 10%), about five times FY26 revenue. As a developer it owns NOPL Solar, a 969 MW AC farm-solar (PM-KUSUM) portfolio in Maharashtra, of which about 45 MW was running by August 2026
capacity.utilisation: Not measured for the EPC business; NOPL had about 45 MW of 969 MW running (about 5%), another 15 MW due within days and about 240 MW at an advanced stage (August 2026)
capacity.fullUse: NOPL at full output: about ₹500–525cr of power sales a year at an 85–89% EBITDA margin (management), under a 25-year agreement with MSEDCL
capacity.capexStatus: Building the 969 MW NOPL solar portfolio: total project cost about ₹4,000cr (Vikran's EPC order ₹3,518cr incl. GST), with ₹1,017cr of central subsidy; debt from IREDA or a Union Bank-led group in final stage (August 2026); completion within 12 months. Vikran paid about ₹10cr for NOPL's equity
capacity.source: Q1 FY27 call (Aug 2026) and sector note

capacity.today: Two leased ships since 23 October 2026: Cordelia Empress (built 1990; 796 cabins, 69 of them suites or balconies; beds for up to 2,005 guests), now home-ported in Kochi, and Cordelia Sky (1,002 cabins, 260 suites or balconies; up to 2,400 guests) sailing from Mumbai. 1,798 cabins in all, about 126% more than Empress alone
capacity.utilisation: Load factor (guests against two per cabin) 91.23% in H1 FY27 (87.79% a year earlier) and 75.53% in Q2 FY27, the monsoon quarter; with extra beds the fleet can run at 115–120%
capacity.capexStatus: Ships are taken on 10-year hire-purchase leases (about US$16m a year for Sky). Sister ship Sun (1,002 cabins) is confirmed for about September–October 2027; about ₹220cr was paid for Sky and Sun from internal accruals before the IPO. ₹429cr has been advanced, through a subsidiary and an unnamed intermediary, towards a fourth ship still under discussion
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (9 Oct 2026), NSE filing of 26 Oct 2026 and sector note

capacity.today: Two plants in Maharashtra, 7,500 panel verticals a year in total: Navi Mumbai (21,500 sq ft, full manufacturing, 5,350) and Pune (12,500 sq ft, assembly only, 2,150). It made 6,553 verticals in FY26
capacity.utilisation: About 95% at both plants in H1 FY27 (CFO, 28 Oct 2026 call); in FY26, Navi Mumbai 94.4% and Pune 70% (presentation)
capacity.fullUse: Not stated in sales. At FY26's roughly ₹3 lakh of revenue per vertical (my calculation), the 22,500 verticals after Ambernath could support about ₹650cr a year
capacity.capexStatus: Ambernath (Thane) plant for 15,000 verticals a year (14,300 LV, 700 MV), costing ₹66.4cr, being installed. Phase 1 (about 5,000) from end-November 2026, subject to pollution-board consent and a fire NOC; the rest by end-December 2026; full use in 12–18 months. About ₹34cr of capex spent in H1 FY27
capacity.source: H1 FY27 call (28 Oct 2026), H1 FY27 and Sep 2026 presentations, RHP (Mar 2026)

capacity.today: Metal powders 620 t a year (600 t water-atomised, 20 t gas-atomised); tungsten heavy alloys 60 t a year after a new furnace (up from 18 t); Swastik Tungsten (57.5% owned) 120 t a year of tungsten powder (10 t a month), restarted in 2026
capacity.utilisation: H1 FY27: powders 256 t in six months (about 43 t a month against about 52 t installed; the MD gives a run rate of 50 t a month and aims for 100); tungsten alloys 2–2.5 t a month against 5 t; Swastik about 2 t a month against 10 t. The company calls about 75% the practical peak use
capacity.fullUse: The MD says today's set-up plus small additions can reach ₹400–500cr of sales; he agreed with an analyst that the tungsten alloy line at full use is worth about ₹150cr at current prices
capacity.capexStatus: H1 FY27 capex ₹7cr from profits, bank lines and 30% advances on export orders. Company roadmap (tentative): powders 620 → 800 t in FY27 → 1,350 t in FY28 (larger water atomiser ordered, 600 → 1,200 t; gas atomisation 20 → 50 → 150 t) → about 1,600 t with the DRDO-funded ₹8.73cr 100 kg gas atomiser (FY28 install); tungsten 18 → 180 t in FY27 (alloys 60 t + Swastik 120 t), alloys to about 90 t in about two years. A spark plasma sintering furnace is being bought from Germany (advance paid). An EIGA atomiser for titanium and zirconium powders is being evaluated. ₹37.5cr of preferential issues committed (₹14cr received), mainly for working capital; the MD says current plants are funded and only a greenfield plant for the ₹1,000cr vision would need new money. The June call had said there was no significant capex plan for FY27–FY28
capacity.source: H1 FY27 call (3 Nov 2026) and presentation, Q4 FY26 call (3 Jun 2026), FY26 annual report

capacity.today: Seven aerospace factories in the UK (Nasmyth and Bromford; sites include Nottingham, Leicester, Coventry, Bournemouth and Worthing) and plants in India at Hyderabad (defence electronics) and Sri City (aerospace parts and ammunition): about 350,000 sq ft and 800+ staff in all. Sri City phase 1 is 75,000 sq ft with 100,000 machining hours a year, budgeted to reach about 300,000 hours in the same building
capacity.utilisation: India aerospace capacity about 15% used, ammunition about 20%, defence electronics on a single shift (CEO, 6 Nov 2026 call)
capacity.capexStatus: Management says the capex already made covers the next few years. About £8–9m went into the UK plants (machines, automation and working capital); fixed-asset spending was ₹60cr in FY26 (Screener) and about ₹61cr in H1 FY27. The rest of the 23-acre, 500,000 sq ft Sri City campus is to be running within about 12 months of September 2026; no cost is disclosed. Growth beyond that is planned through acquisitions funded by up to ₹3,000cr of new equity
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (6 Nov 2026), Q2 FY27 presentation, press release of 10 Sep 2026, Q1 FY27 presentation (Aug 2026)

capacity.today: Fabless: no factories of its own. Pilot units are built at its Bengaluru R&D centre (with an in-house clean room); volume production is outsourced to Kaynes Technology and Avalon Technology under non-exclusive contracts. Capacity is the partners' and is not stated in units
capacity.utilisation: Not disclosed. The CBO said supplying large volumes is not a concern, and the CFO said common sub-assemblies are kept in stock so tactical orders can be delivered in 3–4 months
capacity.capexStatus: No plant capex (property, plant and equipment about ₹23cr). Spending goes to R&D: about ₹30cr in FY27, of which about ₹25cr capitalised, plus the ₹160cr first high-power microwave (directed-energy) system over about 2.5 years, funded by a ₹120cr EXIM Bank loan, a ₹25cr iDEX Aditi grant and ₹15cr of its own money
capacity.source: Q2 FY27 call (6 Nov 2026), RHP (Oct 2026), Q2 FY27 results

capacity.today: Asset-light: no plants; capacity is people. 500+ staff across the group (FY26 presentation), including 222 permanent staff in the Indian parent (March 2026) and 200+ professionals in Japan, working from Pune, Hyderabad, Tokyo and the US. Softenger would add about 1,200 people (combined 1,600+, October 2026 presentation)
capacity.utilisation: Not disclosed. Management says it cut the bench at IM Corp in Q2 FY27 by sharing staff across Fidel and IM accounts
capacity.capexStatus: No plant capex; Screener shows ₹9.45cr of fixed assets bought in FY26, not explained on the calls. The money goes to acquisitions: about ₹22cr paid for the FY26 deals (Fidel Technologies KK, Techvine, IM Corp), funded partly by ₹16cr of yen loans, and Softenger agreed for about ₹38.5cr (cash plus about ₹8cr in shares), due to complete by 31 December 2026. 3–5% of revenue goes to in-house or joint R&D and start-up investments
capacity.source: H1 FY27 call (30 Oct 2026), FY26 and Q2 FY27 presentations, FY26 annual report, NSE filing of 30 Oct 2026
